Oṃ uṃ, salutation to the lunar maṇḍala, whose self consists of sixteen digits.
Having struck that substance with *darbha* grass, it is veiled with the syllable Huṃ.
The practitioner should display the dhenu-mudrā with the syllable "vaṃ."
Having taken up the incense, one should offer it with the syllable *oṃ*. Having understood *namo* as *hsauḥ*, one should write it for the sake of the cause: *hsauḥ hkṣauḥ*. || 17 ||
One should fashion three lines according to the sequence beginning with *a* and *ka*;
one should write *halakṣaṃ* in the corner, and *hsauḥ* and *hkṣauḥ* in its center.
Now, regarding the characteristics of the mantra *hsauḥ*:
in the Nārāyaṇītantra, the Goddess said: "O Lord, the consonant is declared to be the Puruṣa (the Person), and the vowel is the Śakti (Power)."
O Mahādeva, how is it that two liṅgas are joined together within a single power?
Śrī Mahādeva said:
The great subtle *ekaliṅga* is the syllable *ha* situated in the middle of the mantra;
the gross *liṅga* is the syllable *sa*, which is also situated in the middle of the syllable *ha*.
By the fourteenth vowel, the two bodies become one body;
by the sixteenth vowel, the sixteen digits (kalās) are increased.
Having abandoned that which is full of decay, this fourteen-fold mantra adorned with *hsauḥ* is proclaimed; the *visarga* is said to be the activity. || 22 ||
The half-sound of *nāda*, which is the half of the letter *ha*, is revealed as the location of the *yantra*;
in its center is the Great Liṅga, which is also the remainder of the letter *ha*. (23)
Below that is the letter *sa*, conjoined with the Power (*śakti*), which signifies masculinity [or full awakening];
it should be known as the fourteenth vowel, which bestows both hands and feet upon the two.
O Śivā, the thirteenth is to be known as the hand and the fourteenth as the foot;
O Supreme Goddess, one should contemplate the self of desire as the visarga.
The letter *sa* was joined with the letter *ha*, and the letter *ha* with the letter *sa*;
where the subtlety of these two [merged], the fourteenth syllable, the *praṇava*, came into being.
Half of a *bindu*, one *bindu*, half of a *bindu*, and the supreme *kalā*;
the second syllable of the triad is spoken with the resonance of *kalā-nāda*.
In the midst of that is the great void (*mahāśūnya*), which is the *praṇava* as declared by the Vedas. (27)
In Nigamānanda, Śrī Śiva said:
"O Goddess, you are the supreme, eternal bestower of both enjoyment and liberation.
Now I wish to hear the characteristics of the *h-kṣau* mantra. (28)
The Śrī Devī said:
The letter *ha* is indeed the seed-syllable (*bīja*) of Śiva; the letter *ṣa* consists of the quality of *rajas*;
and by means of the letter *ka*, the letter *ṣa* becomes the letter *kṣa*, cherished by desire.
Accompanied by the syllable *kamala*,
joined with the fourteen vowels, and ending with *hkṣau*— this is proclaimed as the mantra.
This mantra, consisting of Śiva and Śakti, is spoken in the form of the *rajas* quality.
The letter Ṣa is the nature of passion (rajas), and the letter Ha is spoken of as the nature of passion. || 30 ||
The letter *śa* three times is the form of Śakti, adorned with the three qualities (*guṇas*). Sattva, rajas, and tamas are to be known as the threefold manifestation of the one supreme Śakti. (31)
In the Kulārṇava:
having projected a triangle outside of that, one should mutter the two mantras ten times each.
The mantra is as follows:
Hrīṃ klīṃ, O Supreme Mistress, O Carrier of the Void of the Supreme Space, O Devourer of the Moon, Sun, and Fire, enter the vessel, svāhā!
Ai Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! We know Ānandeśvara; we meditate upon Sudhādevī; may that Urdhvanārīśvara inspire us.
Then, one should perform the rite of liberation from curses (śāpamocana).
Oṃ! There is only one supreme Brahman, eternal and consisting of both the gross and the subtle;
by that [Brahman], I destroy the sin of killing a Brahmin born from my mental essence (kaca). || 32 ||
Oṃ! O Goddess, born from the solar disc, arisen from the abode of Varuṇa, consisting of the seed-syllable *amā*, may [this] be released from the curse of Śukra. 33.
Oṃ! If the Praṇava is the seed of the Vedas and consists of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Goddess, may it remove your sin of killing a Brahmin. (34)
Having held the jar and recited the three mantras three times,
one shall release [the recipient] from the curse of Kṛṣṇa, the curse of Śukra, and the curse of Brahmā.
The Goddess said: "O Lord of Gods, by drinking liquor one will indeed attain divinity;
since liquor is thus a seed [of divinity], tell me, why is there a curse in that regard? (36)
(p. 99) Śrī Mahādeva said—
in the Gautamīya:
Amṛta is that which is conjoined with śakti; for that devoid of śakti is merely intoxicating. In the drinking of liquor devoid of śakti, Śukra, Brahmā, and Janārdana [are present]. (37)
O Eternal One, having caused confusion regarding the quality of the substance, one may utter a curse;
thereafter, O Supreme Goddess, having cast off that curse, one should drink the honey.
Then one should mutter each mantra ten times even for the sake of the causal rite;
this substance, which releases one from curses and other afflictions, is difficult to obtain even for the gods. (39)
Now, the release from the curses:
O Maheśvarī, for the sake of being released from the curse of Brahmā, the curse of Śukra, and the curse of Kṛṣṇa,
one should recite the mantra three times for the purpose of release and ten times for the underlying cause.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vaiṃ vauṃ vaḥ, obeisance to the goddess Sudhā, who is liberated from the curse of Brahmā.
Thus ends the release from the curse of Brahmā.
*Oṃ śāṃ śīṃ śūṃ śaiṃ śauṃ śaḥ*, salutation to the Goddess Sudhā, who has been liberated from the curse of Śukra. Thus ends the release from the curse of Śukra.

Oṃ hrīḥ aiḥ hrīḥ śrīṃ krāṃ krīṃ krūṃ kraiṃ krauṃ kraḥ sudhe, release the curse of Kṛṣṇa, cause the nectar to flow, cause it to flow, svāhā! [In some recensions, the reading is: klāḥ klīḥ klūḥ klaḥ klauḥ klaḥ. This is the release from the curse of Kṛṣṇa.
In the Vīra-tantra:
having meditated upon Ānandabhairava, and likewise upon Ānandabhairavī.
Likewise, the hero should worship Bhairavī named Ānandā three times in the midst of the substances with perfumes ground into a paste. 41.
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter in the Sarvollāsa composed by the illustrious Sarvānandanātha. || 0 ||
The Twenty-sixth Chapter.
In the Vīra-tantra, likewise, Ānandabhairavī said:
"O Beloved of my life, tell me of that meditation which is supreme bliss. (1)
Śrī Śiva said:
Now, the meditation on Ānandabhairava:
[He who is] resplendent like ten million suns and as cooling as ten million moons.
The god has eighteen arms, five faces, and three eyes. || 2 ||
Seated in the midst of the ocean of nectar, established upon a Brahma-lotus,
mounted on a bull, blue-throated, and adorned with all ornaments.
The god holds a skull and a khaṭvāṅga staff, sounds a bell and a ḍamaru drum,
and wields a noose, a goad, a mace, and a club.
Holding a sword, a shield, a paṭṭiśa, a mallet, a trident, and a staff, he carries a lance and a severed head, with hands displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
The best of practitioners should meditate upon Lohita, the Lord of the Gods of gods; having thus visualized him, he should worship Ānandabhairava in the midst of the ritual substances. (6)
The mantra is:
*oṃ ha sa kṣa ma la va ra yūṃ ānandabhairavāya vaṣaṭ*.
One should first worship Bhairava three times, and thereafter Bhairavī.
Bhairavī is the embodiment of wine; Bhairava is the embodiment of bliss. || 7 ||
Now, the meditation on Ānandabhairavī:
One should contemplate the goddess Surā,
possessing the radiance of ten million times ten thousand moons.
White as a snow-mountain or the moon, she has five faces and three eyes. || 8 ||
Endowed with eighteen arms, intent on bestowing all bliss,
subduing the planets, large-eyed, she stood facing the God of gods.
Having meditated thus, one should worship three times.
The mantra is:
Oṃ ha sa kṣa ma la va ra yīṃ, vauṣaṭ to Sudhādevī [or Ānandabhairavī].
One should worship the Goddess three times, according to the distinction of the three qualities (guṇas).
In the *Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi*:
"Alternatively, I shall describe the purification of substances in another manner.
In the *Nigamakalpadruma*, Śrī Śiva said:

The manifold purification of substances, which is approved for various states of being, cannot be fully explained even in a hundred lifetimes. Among those [purifications], by what means should a practitioner perform the rite of accomplishment? (11)
(p. 102) Now, the abbreviated purification.
The venerable Goddess said:
Within the substances, the syllable of the Mother (Mātṛkā) with the nasal drop (bindu) bestows happiness and liberation;
each letter is joined with the drop and adorned by the Bindu and Nāda.
O Maheśvara, even in the counter-clockwise direction, one should draw that same color within the triangles;
one should write the form of the triangle beginning with 'A', 'Ka', and 'Tha' in due order.
One should write the fifty letters in a counter-clockwise direction within the circle of jewels;
the syllables *ha*, *la*, *kṣaṃ* are situated in the three triangles, which are of the nature of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.
Śrī Śiva said: In which corner does Brahmā reside? In which corner does Janārdana reside? In which corner does Śambhu reside? Tell me, O beloved of my life. (15)
The Śrī Devī said:
In the lower portion of the first corner resides Brahmā, the agent of creation;
in the middle corner dwells Viṣṇu, the stainless protector.
In the final corner is Mahādeva, who is one with Prakṛti in a single body.
Now, the purification of substances by another method:

Śiva is to be known as having the form of the *bindu*, and Caṇḍikā as having the form of the *nāda*. The wise man should draw the *pīṭha* consisting of *nāda* and *bindu* in the midst of the substance. 17.
Having written the supreme [syllable] which possesses three sounds, is impelled by the three powers, has three points, and is the three deities— [O Beloved, it is dear to the three Śivas]—
one should contemplate the substance as being devoid of the state of death.
Now he speaks of another method:
"O God, whatever mantra the practitioner constantly recites in the presence of the Guru,
with that very mantra, the substance is consecrated seven times."
By reciting [the mantra] seven times, the purification of substances occurs at that very moment.
Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter in the Sarvollāsa composed by Śrī Sarvānandanātha. || 0 ||
The Twenty-Seventh Chapter. Now, the characteristics of the *māṃsa* [flesh].
In the *Kularahasya*:
Wine bestows sovereignty, and sexual union bestows liberation;
the supreme Greatness of the three qualities (guṇatrayamahat) should be known as the cause of both.
Meat, fish, and the *mudrā* are proclaimed as the threefold [cause]; for they are indeed the cause of the cause, the great bliss of sexual union. (2)
And meat is said to be of three kinds: that which moves in water, on land, and in the sky;
namely, that of the pigeon, the goat, and the tortoise, O Supreme Goddess. (3)
Having diligently brought these three kinds of meat—those of creatures of the air, the earth, and the water—for the sake of pleasing the Goddess, [he offered them]. (4)
In the *Yāmala*:
"Meats are indeed of three kinds: those that move in the air, on the earth, and in the water."
Having brought them with effort, he should have them killed for the sake of the Goddess.
O Mother, because of killing in the place designated for the Goddess, there is no sin; O beautiful one, otherwise,
by killing elsewhere, O Goddess, one would go to the Raurava hell.
In the Kulārṇava it is said:
"O Dear One, the killing of living beings for one's own sake is never enjoined;
however, the killing of living beings is prescribed in sacrifices to the ancestors and the gods. (7)
O Supreme Goddess, he who kills a living being without authorization will undoubtedly fall into a difficult, inaccessible, and terrible place. || 8 ||
One should never cut even a blade of grass without a purpose;
yet, having killed for the sake of a deity or for the sake of a twice-born, one is not tainted by sin.
On the island of knowledge (jñānadvīpa), one should never cut down even a blade of grass without a specific injunction; yet,
having destroyed [beings] for the sake of the deity or for the sake of the twice-born, one is not tainted by sins.
Even by killing a Brahmin or a cow according to the prescribed rite, one is not tainted by sins;
nevertheless, O Supreme Goddess, this does not bring auspiciousness to the wise,
because the majesty and fruit of the five elements (pañcatattva) are fivefold.
Now, the purification of meat:
one should cast some substance into the meat placed within the maṇḍala;
by reciting the mantra three times, the purification of the meat occurs instantly. (12)
The mantra is:
Oṃ, Viṣṇu is praised for his heroic power— he who is like a fearsome beast, roaming on the mountains.
In whose three strides all the worlds abide upon his two thighs. || 13 ||

O Maheśānī, one should recite this mantra three times over the meat [or mutter it]; one should cause a piece of meat mixed with liquor to be offered into the mouth of the Śakti. Now, the characteristics of the fish:
In the *Kulatatvasāra*:
"The *illīśa*, *kabajī*, *śāla*, *vācā*, *śakuna*, *proṣṭhikā*, *sadguru*, *vodāla*, and *rohita*—these are the most excellent, O Dear One. (15)
O Maheśvarī, whatever other fish there may be that are pleasing to women, they should be offered, provided they have been thoroughly cleaned, into the mouth of Śakti.
Fish and meat should indeed be offered, especially when fried;
therefore, O woman of excellent complexion, it should be known that what is roasted is highly praised.
In another tantra:
"If meat and fish are to be purified so as to be pleasing to women, they should be offered into the mouth of the Śakti, accompanied by the [proper] causal rite. (18)
Now, the purification of the fish:
Oṃ, we worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity;
may he deliver us from death as one delivers a cucumber from its stem, [delivering us] unto immortality. 19.
O Dear One, one should place a fish upon the maṇḍala and cast it in according to the causal rites;
by reciting the mantra three times, the purification of the fish occurs at that very moment.
(p. 106) Now, the characteristics of the *mudrā*:
parched rice is said to be [offered] with sugar and other such substances.
It is well-perfumed;
this is proclaimed as the characteristic of the cluster of lotuses of the womb. || 21 ||
O Maheśvarī, other substances may be roasted [or consumed];
if the mudrā is thus purified, it is supremely pleasing to the Goddess.
"O Maheśvarī, grain parched by contact with fire is to be chewed"—this is the gesture (mudrā) known as the bestower of great joy. (23)
Now, the purification of the mudrās:
one should place the mudrā upon the maṇḍala and cast it down with the causal [mantra].
Having recited the two mantras three times, the purification of the mudrās occurs at that very moment. (24)
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ. The wise ever behold that supreme abode of Viṣṇu, like an eye fixed in the heavens. 1.
Oṃ! The wise, ever-vigilant and full of inspired praise, kindle that which is the supreme station of Viṣṇu. || 2 ||
Thus concludes the purification of the mudrās.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter in the Sarvollāsa composed by Śrī Sarvānandanātha.
The Twenty-Eighth Chapter. In the *Kulārṇava*:
"With a thousand loads of wealth and hundreds of loads of meat..."
Without power, nothing can be accomplished; therefore, one should take recourse in power. || 1 ||
Now, the definition of a consort (*śakti*).
In the *Yāmala*:
"One's own consort or another's consort, having been initiated in the presence of the Guru..."
Abiding there, she is that Śakti whose essence is divine, worshipped by all.
Having diligently brought a Śakti who is well-behaved and sweet-spoken,
adorned with a red cloth, either in front of the Guru or to his left,
the excellent practitioner should then embellish her with many ornaments.
In the *Vṛhad-yonitantra*:
"O Goddess, having brought a beloved woman who is well-behaved, sweetly smiling, devoted to the Guru, and intent upon the Kula practice... (4)

O Maheśvarī, having brought with great effort a consecrated woman, another’s beloved, or one’s own mother— a Śakti endowed with the bliss of the Tattvas and cherished within the supreme principles— one should not observe distinctions of caste.
One should bring into the center of the circle a woman who is devoid of compassion and shame, always filled with joy, or one who is exhilarated by drinking.
In the *Kālikākalpa*:
"One should worship one's chosen goddess within the *cakra*, [visualizing] one's own wife as the beloved consort;
or else, having fashioned the *yantra* near a woman, one should perform the worship. (7)
In another tantra:
"Having recognized that women are the very form of one's own chosen deity, worship should be performed."
A yantra was fashioned near him out of respect for his command.
In the *Jñānārṇava*:
"O Supreme Goddess, when worship and recitation are performed in the presence of a woman, it is declared that the imperishable fruit is a hundred times greater than that of Kāmarūpa. (9)
One must not speak of her defects or lack of power, for she is of the very nature of the Goddess;
and one should not perform a purification rite for her, as she is a Brahmin devoted to the Kula. 10.
Since there is no purification of one's own power and yet both possess a single self,
one should purify the supreme power for the sake of attaining oneness from duality.
If the nature of the object to be accomplished were foolishly identical with the nature of the accomplisher,
then purification would not need to be performed, just as the water of the Ganges is already pure.
Just as [impurity] in the Gaṅgā [is not considered a fault]. || 12 ||
Expiation must be performed wherever the Gaṅgā does not reside;
purification of one's power must be performed when the Self is not united with Śiva.
O Goddess, O Maheśvarī, when there is oneness of self between the seeker and the goal, then through the purity of the self comes the purity of power; for such a one, success is not far off.

In the Nigamakalpa, the illustrious Mahādeva said: "When one is a solitary practitioner, possessing a single state of being, and deluded by singular joys, where then can there be any fault in Śakti? For one's own absorption occurs right there."
If one should perform the purification of Śakti without knowing the reality of the Kula,
by the mere knowledge of which one certainly becomes full-bliss,
how can there be purification for him, O auspicious lady, if he merely contemplates it with the mind? (16)
The Śrī Devī said:
O Supreme Lord, [tell me] regarding the Kula in the right, the left, and the middle.
Through knowledge, the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, and Sarasvatī always appear as water. || 17 ||
The power (śakti) would be distinguished by these [attributes], and the body would consist of the deity.
O God, if that [body] were impure, then the deity would also be impure. (18)
O Maheśvara, for the ignorant, purification always occurs through mantras and the like;
yet if there is no purification of the mind, then purification by mantra is very far indeed.
In the Kālītantra:
"If a woman who has not received initiation worships within the center of the cakra, yet does not worship the complete cakra there, then she will not attain full bliss. (20)
Therefore, one should worship the well-characterized Śakti and those who have been initiated;
having prostrated with the thought that she is the deity, one should cause the vessel of enjoyment to be offered. || 21 ||
O Maheśvarī, the vessel for enjoyment should not be given to a widow;
rather, one should worship a widow who has high breasts and is devoted to the pleasure of love.
O Maheśvarī, he who places the vessel of enjoyment into the hand of a widow shall,
having bypassed her womb, offer that essence to the Goddess.
O Supreme Goddess, out of fear or shame one should not perform the ritual;
both [the teacher and the disciple] would suffer greatly, being bound by the fetters of the individual soul (paśu-pāśa). // 24 //
And by her command, he should cause the widow to engage in sexual intercourse;
the emission of semen should be performed according to her word. (25)
As long as there is no emission of semen within the circle of the widow’s womb, so long should one engage in dalliance; at the end of the emission, one should desist. || 26 ||
p.

110) When the emission of semen occurs and the Command (ājñā) of the Śakti does not arise, one should indeed consume [the substance] after offering it with the mantra prescribed by the Kāraṇa, O Śivā. (27)
Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter in the *Sarvollāsa* composed by the venerable Sarvānandanātha. || 0 ||
The Twenty-Ninth Chapter.
The Holy Goddess said:
[O Lord,] that virtuous Śakti, who consists of Brahman, is free from desire and compassionate toward her devotees.
[To her who is] affectionate toward her devotees:
Tell me, how is her initiation described, or how is she a widow? || 1 ||
Śrī Śiva said:
Power (Śakti) devoid of bliss is of two kinds and is uninitiated;
she becomes worthy of worship through bliss—she who possesses bliss is adored by heroes.
Having performed the great wheel there, one should wipe the body with the hand;
she should be known as initiated and a married woman if she has resorted to bliss.
O Maheśvarī, the Śakti endowed with the state of a Vīra is the consort of Śiva;
the Śākta endowed with the state of a Vīra is none other than Śiva himself—of this there is no doubt.
Having realized "I am Śiva," one should delight in the Śrīcakra along with the Śivā.
In the Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi:
"O Great Goddess, when the Self is blissful, the world consists of all-bliss;
when the Self is pure, the world is pure, and when it is impure, it is likewise impure. (5)
In the *Nārāyaṇītantra*:
"Since Brahman [or O Goddess], the purification of Śakti need not be performed."
She is of the nature of the self;
even when the self is impure, she is impure, just as there is a coloring upon a crystal.
Nevertheless, though constrained by the bonds of the individual soul (paśu), one must remain pure;
O Great Goddess, the practitioner never takes upon himself the fault of the Śakti.
Your form also possesses power, since it is the bestower of liberation; endowed with both enjoyment and liberation, one who follows the Śākta path should not commit any fault against that power.
In the *Śrī Kālītantra* (as seen in the two manuscripts gh and j):

"One must never harbor hatred toward women; rather, one should especially perform worship of women. One should avoid striking them, censuring them, being deceitful toward them, or acting unpleasantly. (9)
Under no circumstances should this be done otherwise, for it would obstruct success;
women are the gods, women are the vital breaths, and women alone are the ornament.
One should always remain attached to women; otherwise, even toward one's own wife, [one will feel aversion].
[For her] flowers are plucked by her hand, and water is drawn by her hand. (11)
The best of practitioners, girt with the great silk-tree creeper, should offer the substance gathered by his hand to the deities. (12)
If one recites the mantra at night, what could be difficult for him to attain? And what is the fruit of being entwined by the vines of the great *cīna* tree? (13)
Those corpses do not equal even a sixteenth part of this;
entering the vine-cottage yields a fruit far greater than sitting upon a corpse-seat. (14)
One who desires enjoyments, deluded by the pleasures of enjoyment, should purify the *śakti*;
likewise, one deluded by the pleasures of desire through conversation and the touch of the body.
O Goddess, without the bliss of desire, neither enjoyment nor liberation arises for one who is deluded. 15.
Even though this purification exists both for the wise through knowledge and for the ignorant through mantra,
nevertheless, among the wise, even that man who possesses the highest knowledge must perform the purification of Śakti, O Dear One, because she is composed of his own chosen deity.
Now follows the purification of the *śakti*:
having washed it with fragrant waters and perfumed it with excellent incenses,
and having colored it with vermilion, one should write the root mantra upon the vulva (*bhaga*).
O Ambikā, one should perform the immediate consecration for women who have not been initiated;
through the ritual procedure of mantra-initiation, the purification of their power (śakti) occurs at that very moment.
In the Kulārṇava:
"O Maheśānī, one should extract the Māyā-bīja into the left ear of those who are uninitiated; having worshipped them, one should cause the vessel of enjoyment (bhogapātra) to be offered. (19)
The purification as stated in the *Yāmala*:
one should perform the entire network of nyāsas prescribed for one's own ritual manual upon the body of the Śakti;
having sprinkled her with red flowers, one should join her at the region of the *yoni*. 20.
Oṃ, salutation; then the seed-syllable Vāgbhava, followed by Māyā and Lakṣmī;
then the word "Tripurādevī" is extracted with the vocative case ending. (21)
One should recite ten times: "imāṃ [ch: imāṃ śaktiṃ paritrāṇaṃ kru kuru mama śaktiṃ kuru kuru svāhā]. Then, one should utter the word "pavitrīkuru" (purify) after the word "śaktiṃ."
One should mutter ten times: "Make my power [victorious] in the duel, svāhā! (mama śaktiṃ kuru dvandvaṃ svāhā). || 22 ||
"pavitrīkuru mama śaktiṃ kuru kuru svāhā.
O Śivā, one should worship that Goddess according to the prescribed rite with the five elements (pañcatattva).
When the vessel of enjoyment is to be given, then one should practice sexual union. || 23 ||
In the *Guptasādhanatantra*, the venerable Goddess said:
"The purification of all substances and so forth has been revealed in many ways. O Lord, for the benefit of the world, please explain that pure [method] in brief. (24)
Śrī Śiva said: Whatever mantra a man (or practitioner) constantly recites with the light of the Guru, [that is his true mantra].
O Goddess, one should perform the six-limbed ritual placement (nyāsa) using that very mantra. || 25 ||
Having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa), the mantra-practitioner should then consecrate the substances and other materials;
having performed the consecration seven times, everything will certainly become purified.
O beautiful one, having offered the Guru, Śiva, and likewise the Goddess, as well as the sacrificial offering itself, one should perform the oblation into the mouth of Kuṇḍalinī with the root mantra.
O Goddess, O Great Mistress, the Kuṇḍalinī, the supreme deity, resides in the Mūlādhāra; at the time of enjoyment, one should contemplate her extending as far as the tip of the tongue. 28.
Having carefully covered the purified fish, meat, and other offerings with his mouth,
he should recite the root mantra and offer them into the mouth of Kuṇḍalī.
The wise one should act in this manner for every vessel and every morsel;
thus, his desire for food ceases, and he who is called "the living soul" remains unstained.
He goes to a terrible hell together with twenty-one generations of his lineage. (31)
Having worshipped the gods and the ancestors according to the path prescribed by the family scriptures, one who drinks liquor and eats meat while remembering the Guru incurs no fault. 32.
He who consumes wine and other such substances for the sake of pleasure is a sinner;
however, one who is free from desire should partake of them for the propitiation of the deity.
Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter in the *Sarvollāsa* composed by Śrī Sarvānandanātha.
The Thirty-first Chapter. In the *Samayācāra-tantra*:
"Having performed the grasping of consciousness, that is the cause immediately thereafter."
For consciousness is indeed conceived as the cause of the cause. || 1 ||
The Śrī Devī said:
O Mahādeva, what is consciousness? O Lord, tell me, what is its cause?
Why is drinking the cause, such that a person partakes in the bliss of consciousness?
Now begins the section on Sambidā.
The illustrious Śiva said:
"O Śivā, the practitioner (sādhaka) is of two kinds: one who is empowered by internal disposition (bhāvaśakta) and one who is powerless (aśakta)."
It is permeated by existence, the bliss of consciousness, the bliss of wine, and non-duality.

O auspicious lady, a man who possesses being (*bhāva*) through being, yet is deluded by the joys of worldly existence (*bhāva*), becomes a partaker of liberation, O Queen of Gods, through the joys of being (*bhāva*). (4)
O Maheśvarī, at the beginning and the end, there is the drinking of consciousness by means of the cause;
then liberation as absolute oneness (kaivalya) shall occur—this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
Sālokya, sārūpya, and sāyujya— O Supreme Goddess,
this knowledge arising from direct realization is endowed with both for the sake of liberation.

In the *Nigamatattva*, the venerable Goddess said: "O Maheśāna, for him in whose body bliss (*ānanda*)— the very form of Brahman— is established, everything is the bliss of perfection (*siddhyānanda*)."
which bestows eternal bliss. || 7 ||
For every meditation performed without bliss (or, according to variant *gh*: without wine) is entirely fruitless;
therefore, O Mahādeva, one should practice the grasping of consciousness (*saṃvid*).
Whether he be an ascetic or even a king, O Supreme Lord, he may at times seek the bliss of wine,
but [he should always seek] the bliss of spiritual perfection (siddhi) here and there.
O God, it increases the bliss of consciousness for other practitioners at all times; on certain festival days, it is accompanied by the joy of wine and the drinking of honey.
One should drink wine during the dark fortnight; during the bright fortnight, one should joyfully drink for the sake of accomplishment.
If one drinks wine during the bright fortnight, one should drink at the beginning and end for the sake of consciousness.
In another Tantra it is said:
"O Śivā, one should drink wine conjoined with consciousness during the dark fortnight;
during the bright fortnight, one should drink the first [liquor], and for the sake of accomplishment, one should drink honey during the dark fortnight. (12)
In the *Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi*:
"The arising of *sattva* belongs to *Sambidā*, that which arises from *rajas* belongs to *Madya*, and that which arises from *tamas* belongs to *Tvaritā*; such is the characteristic of bliss. (13)
O Supreme Goddess, even though it exists as mere being, it is devoid of action.
The *rājasī* [nature] possesses the power of action; the *tāmasī* [nature] is devoid of action. || 14 ||
O Supreme Goddess, just as there is no bliss from wine without its potency (śakti), so too, O Goddess, the bliss of wine is certainly not attained without spiritual accomplishment (siddhi). 15.
O Maheśvarī, one should first drink the *samaya* [wine], then the *madya*;
thereafter, one should worship the Śakti in the *cakra*, and then joyfully drink the *siddhi*.
O Maheśānī, without *siddhi* one is not a practitioner of yoga in the work of the Kula;
therefore, O Maheśvarī, one who is joined with Śakti should drink the *siddhi*.
Indeed, that drinking which is devoid of power is proclaimed as *sambidā*;
at its conclusion, when joined with power, it becomes the *samaya* through *sambidā*. (18)
O Goddess, when there is sexual union, then she becomes Vijayā;
even in the practice of one's own will, the union is free from prohibitions and injunctions. (19)
Then that goddess, the eternal consciousness and the means of accomplishment, having diligently gathered the substance arising from Śiva, became Śakti. || 20 ||
Then that goddess Saṃvidā, who is of a fragile form and speaks kindly—
O Goddess, he who serves Saṃvidā endowed with the five limbs,
having enjoyed happiness in this world, goes at the end to the supreme goal. || 21 ||
O Goddess, Supreme Sovereign, Sambidā, Samayā, Vijayā, Siddhi, and Bhaṅga— these are proclaimed as the fivefold [names].
He who performs this at the three junctions of the day is undoubtedly equal to me. || 22 ||
Having consumed an intoxicating substance, the practitioner who is devoted to the *kula* will certainly experience my own agitation as soon as he falls into agitation. (23)
Therefore, at the outset, one should practice the service of *sambid* toward Śiva;
between *sambid* and the attendant (*āsava*), *sambid* alone is more important. (24)
When a person, having taken hold of *vijayā* [or *saṃvidā*], performs meditation,
then his form consisting of meditation certainly becomes manifest. (25)

Therefore, having drunk of the spirits of consciousness, one should indeed drink of the Cause thereafter; for between the wine of consciousness and [ordinary] wine, consciousness alone is the more weighty.
Through grasping one is released from what is attained; through meditation, perfection will arise.
By means of meditation, whatever form is the object of meditation bestows eternal liberation through conscious awareness.
Just as one who seeks pleasure always finds joy at home when united with his wife, so too,
O lady of excellent limbs, he who seeks bliss should drink Vijayā during the state of bliss.
One who follows the path of ritual action and possesses the power of action may drink Vijayā even when [the substance] is pure. || 28 ||
Now, the purification of consciousness:
Oṃ! O Consciousness, born of Brahman, daughter of Brahman, ever sinless;
for the sake of the satisfaction of the Bhairavas, be forever pure.
Oṃ, homage to Brahmāṇī, svāhā! || 29 ||

Oṃ! O Goddess who are the refuge of the root of accomplishment, who awakens those of inferior understanding, who brings kings and subjects under control, and who wields a trident against the throats of enemies! Oṃ, homage to Kṣatriyā, svāhā! || 30 ||
Oṃ, O fire blazing with the fuel of ignorance, you who are the form of the flame of the fire of knowledge!
Grant me the oblation of bliss, joy, and perfect knowledge.
Hrīḥ! Homage to Vaiśyā, Svāhā! || 31 ||

Oṃ, I pay homage, I pay homage to you, O Mother who reveals the path of yoga [who bestows it], O Mother victorious over the three worlds; be the giver of the fruit of samādhi. Klīṃ [Hrīṃ], obeisance to Śūdrā, svāhā! || 32 ||
O you who are blissful in the joy of those who rejoice in bliss; O you whose two feet are the state of eternal bliss;
O you who cause exultation and bliss in the root; O you whose very nature is the bliss of consciousness. (33)
Divyā, Vimarṣiṇī, Siddhā, Susiddhā, and Siddhimūlikā;
she is the destroyer of disease, the destroyer of the bonds of the fettered, the destroyer of time, and whose form is awakening.
Manonmanī, Madhu, Drākṣā, Khecarī, Vijayā, and Jayā. || 34 ||
Having praised thus,
and having displayed the *dhenumudrā* and the *yonimudrā* to Śivā with the mantra,
one should recite the root mantra ten times and offer oblations into the mouth of Kuṇḍalī.
O Maheśvarī, one should offer it upon one’s own head to Śrīnātha, to one’s chosen deity, and to the practitioner, and then drink it joyfully while reciting the mantra.
The mantra for the drink is as follows:
(In this regard, the reading from manuscript *gh* is: *oṃ bhaṅge bhaṅge mahābhaṅge mahābhairavi māṃ saṃbhāvaya*).
"Honor me! Speak, speak, O Goddess of Speech! Be firmly established on the tip of my tongue!
O Subduer of all enemies! Svāhā! With this mantra, one should offer oblation into the mouth of Kuṇḍalī. *Oṃ bhaṅge bhaṅge mahābhaṅge mahābhaṅge bhairavāṇām...*
"Paralyze, paralyze! Speak, speak, O Goddess of Speech! Be firmly established on the tip of my tongue! O Subduer of all enemies, svāhā! Thus one should drink.
The Śrī Devī said:
Consciousness is declared to be fourfold according to the distinction of its classes;
consciousness is the supreme Vidyā, the auspicious one who bestows both enjoyment and liberation. (37)
O Sadāśiva, how have you described the division of that bond of birth?
O God, beloved of my life, tell me how its purification is achieved, and what constitutes its impurity. (38)
Śrī Mahādeva said:
Due to the practitioner’s omission of ritual action, he is bound by the fetter of birth.
For the sake of the practice of practitioners, she herself is endowed with a noble birth. || 39 ||
O Queen of the Gods, just as earrings and other ornaments are made of gold in various ways,
so too is consciousness manifold in form through the differentiations of knowledge among the wise.
O Maheśvarī, if there is no fault in the consciousness, there is no excellence;
for the excellence of that which is endowed with fruit is indeed to be known as its very flaw. (41)
The Śrī Devī said:
O Supreme Lord, the Goddess is to be known through consciousness as fourfold;
likewise, reveal my characteristic marks and hymn of praise within my own abode.
Śrī Mahādeva said: If a Brāhmaṇa, accompanied by a cowherd, [obtains] a white flower, otherwise he should drink the knowledge of the Samvidas for the sake of bliss. (43)
O Pārvatī, for a Kṣatriya there is a red flower, and for a Vaiśya it is yellow;
indeed, for a Śūdra it is black. By means of the flower, one may recognize the caste; O Goddess of Gods, one should discern the distinction of castes by the difference in flowers.
In the *Jñānārṇava*, the Śrī Devī said:
"O Lord of Lords, what is my caste, if you have favor toward me?
Speak, speak, O God—[O Great God, speak]—for the sake of the welfare of man."
Śrī Śiva said:
Action based on one’s respective caste is proclaimed to be the "bond of caste.
When action is destroyed and caste is likewise destroyed, one becomes a partaker of liberation.
120) In the Ānandapaṭala, the venerable Śiva said:
[One may perform it] with milk, water, ghee, honey, rock salt, or common salt.
Also with sugar, or even with jaggery, and with ripe plantains as well. || 47 ||
The best of practitioners should accept Vijayā with all those priceless, sweet substances such as ripe mangoes, jackfruit, and the like. (48)
Vijayā, when combined with milk, bestows absolute bliss;
it increases great luster and destroys defects of the eyes and other ailments. || 49 ||
Furthermore, when combined with water, it destroys all indigestion;
when taken with ghee and honey, it brings one under the control of Sarasvatī, the Goddess of Speech. (50)
It bestows supreme eloquence and an exceedingly pure intellect;
it destroys disorders of bile and disorders of phlegm when taken with honey. (51)
With rock salt and common salt it becomes a great bestower of fire;
with sugar or even with jaggery, it destroys colic and eliminates bile.
It pacifies diarrhea, crushes asthma and cough, and wards off the malabsorption syndrome (grahaṇī) arising from undigested wind (āmavāta). || 53 ||
Endowed with all very sweet qualities, it destroys all diseases, bestows strength and nourishment, and grants a melodious voice. || 54 ||
She is the bestower of wisdom and discernment, and the one who reveals the path of ethical conduct.
She is the destroyer of excessive urination, urinary obstruction, and gravel.
Out of affection for you, that which was hidden in all the scriptures has been made manifest. 55.
Then, having accepted the Vijayā [wine], one should worship the Guru in the Sahasrāra;
having uttered the Guru-mantra, one should offer it in the dative case. || 56 ||
Having recited the mantra of the venerable Guru’s sandals, one should prostrate like a staff upon the ground;
then, while muttering the mantra of one's chosen deity, the accomplished practitioner may go about his way.
O Goddess, by practicing in this manner every day for a year,
one then becomes radiant, powerful, eloquent, wise, and pleasing to behold. (58)
By the use of this substance, one will undoubtedly become endowed with beauty and youth, and a repository of various virtues. (59)
Between consciousness (samvit) and liquor (āsava), consciousness alone is more important;
therefore, the best of practitioners should perform the ritual application by means of consciousness alone. (60)
Once a day, twice a day, thrice a day, or five times a day;
or one *tolaka*, two *tolakas*, or even three *tolakas*.

The measure (mātrā) should always be neither less nor more; if the measure is deficient or excessive, the fruit will never be attained. Therefore, one who desires success must perform [the practice] according to the prescribed measure. 62.
All this, the supreme ritual manual (kalpa) of Vijayā, has been told to you;
by her grace, the desired accomplishment will be attained without delay. (63)
This supreme secret, which has been declared for one who has attained his desires and dwells in the inner chamber of the mind,
must never be told to anyone at any time.
O Goddess, you too must perform that according to the prescribed rite.
Śrī Śiva said:
The leaf of Trailokyavijayā fried in ghee along with its seeds,
combined with the three pungents (trikaṭu), the three myrobalans (triphalā), śṛṅgī, kṛṣṇā [or kuṣṭha], dhanyāka, and rock salt (saindhava).
Śaṭhī, tālīśapatra, kakkola, nāgakeśara,
the two types of yamānī, methī, and likewise the two types of jīraka— [these are taken in equal parts; this variant reading is seen in these two manuscripts].
These, taken in equal parts and dried, should be ground into a powder during the Raudra muhūrta.
Having taken these powders and an equal amount of *samvit* powder,
one should add sugar equal to the sum of both and mix them thoroughly. (67)
Having mixed it with an equal fourth part of honey and ghee,
one should grind it again on a stone slab and mix it with the three fragrant substances (trisugandhi).
Having placed them in vessels of gold or other materials before him, he should then perform their purification in due order with four mantras.
O Goddess of the gods, what on this earth cannot be accomplished through its service?
O fair-faced one, there is the perfection of mantra, as well as the perfection of worship and recitation.
O Maheśānī, through service one attains the perfection of knowledge and liberation;
this is the truth, O Maheśānī, the truth, the very truth—of this there is no doubt. (71)
With a heart full by means of this, one should perform recitation and worship;
by a single utterance alone, there shall be as many as a hundred thousand crores.
Thus, O beloved, I have told you that which is the essence of essences, higher than the highest;
it must not be given to just anyone—make this a truth, my dear. (73)
Thus ends the thirtieth chapter in the Sarvollāsa composed by Śrī Sarvānandanātha. || 0 ||
The Thirty-First Chapter:
Now, the characteristics of the vessel-support for the practitioner in the center of the Śrīcakra.
In the Kulārṇava:
[This reading is seen as an addition in manuscript Ch. O Śivā, one should place the vessel upon the support with the mantra;
for if one places the vessel upon a support made of clay, it bestows death. || 1 ||
The support is said to be of three kinds: having six lotuses, or four lotuses;
or else it is circular in shape, triangular, or provided with three lotuses.
Now, regarding the characteristics of the vessel for the practitioner, the *Kulārṇava* states:
"The vessel may be made of gold, gems, glass, or fashioned from pearl or a skull."
And this golden one, which fulfills desires, consists of Viśvāmitra, as does this crystal one. || 3 ||
In the Jñānārṇava:
"The hero should draw a triangular mandala and a quadrangular one upon the ground;
he should place a support there and set the vessel upon it. (4)

O Pārvatī, [the vessels] may be made of gold, silver, glass, or even pearl; likewise of steel, coconut, copper, or lotus-metal (jalaja); or of brass, bell-metal, or even fish-shaped [vessels]. || 5 ||
The golden [image] is proclaimed and celebrated as bestowing all auspiciousness;
and the silver one, O lady of excellent hips, is the destroyer of all diseases.
In all rites of sorcery (*abhicāra*), a glass vessel is preeminent;
O Supreme Goddess, a pearl vessel is said to bring about the increase of sons.
O Great Goddess, that which is born of water bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
that made of brass destroys all defects, and that made of copper increases one's fame. (8)
O Great Goddess, one should cause an earthen vessel to be given to the Asuras;
however, a human skull is a great vessel and is recommended for all rites.
In the Vārāhī Tantra:
"Vessels made of gold, silver, and copper bring about all accomplishments (siddhis).
O Śivā, for rites of pacification (śāntika), a stone vessel is used; for rites of immobilization (stambhana), one made of clay."
O Śivā, bell-metal (pittala) is to be known for killing, copper for driving away;
a bronze vessel (kāṃsyapātra) for subjugation, and a glass vessel (kācapātra) for causing enmity.
A great vessel made of viśvāmitra metal is difficult to obtain for all rites.
In the Tantra it is said that they are inexhaustible:
"O Dear One, the vessels are made of gold, silver, stone, tortoise-shell, skull, or clay;
also of coconut, conch, and those originating from fish."
And the fish [is worshipped], O Supreme Goddess. || 12 ||
A wise practitioner should fashion a vessel from the bilva tree;
O Goddess, the adept should vary the vessels according to the specific purpose at hand.
The garland and the vessel grant their fruit swiftly in all rites;
the vessel produced from a human skull is proclaimed to be pure. (14)
In the Haṃsamāheśvara [tantra]:
"Among living beings, the human is the most excellent, for he possesses the distinction between dharma and adharma;
a vessel made from his skull would render everything else useless. (15)
O Maheśānī, if one who is deluded regarding dharma and adharma should act as a vessel [for initiation],
one should oneself cut off his head and fashion it into a great vessel.
Even if he is of the lowest birth, a great sinner, young, or free from disease, the bowl produced from his shaven head is proclaimed to be a "great vessel" (mahāpātra). || 17 ||
(125) One should conceive of the great vessel and the great garland as being of one nature;
for the King, O Maheśvarī, is the Teacher, and he is constituted by the great vessel. 18.
A vessel made by cutting it oneself is [proper]; one who has it made by another becomes a sinner.
Indeed, that vessel which is shaped like a womb is the very form of a great vessel;
it is a vessel that brings me joy and bestows joy upon the practitioner. || 19 ||
O lady of beautiful hips, O auspicious one, the vulva-vessel is the most excellent of great vessels;
who on the surface of the earth knows its majesty apart from you? (20)
Indeed, there is no defect in the womb; one should not perform a purification for it. Without the vessel of the womb, one may drink the honey after having purified the vessel.
For a vessel that has not been purified brings only suffering. (21)
Now, regarding the purification of the vessel (*pātraśuddhi*). In the *Samayācāra-tantra*:
"O Maheśānī, even a mere vessel serves as a substitute for the *yoni-pātra*."
O Maheśānī, when the womb is impure, even the vessel alone is impure.
O Goddess, if there be knowledge of the Yoni, then everything—whether seen, touched, smelled, served, or tasted like honey—becomes pure. (23)
O Śivā, having established the vessel with the root mantra, one should perform the rite of inspection with the root mantra.
O Śivā, one should draw the seed-syllable of Śakti in the center, situated within a triangle;
one should fill it [or worship it], according to the words of the Guru, with the causal [mantra] and the root mantra. (24)
Alternatively, O Maheśānī, all the vessels have been filled according to the general procedure for the arghya offering, O Maheśvarī, by means of the causal principle.
Thus ends the purification of the vessel.
Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the Sarvollāsa composed by the illustrious Sarvānandanātha. || 0 ||
The Thirty-Second Chapter:
Now, the placement of the practitioner’s vessel within the Śrīcakra.
In the Yoginītantra:
To the west of the Śrīpātra, facing the deity of the Cakra (or the wheel of deities),
one should place all the vessels according to the procedure for the general arghya offering.
In the *Kālikākulasarvasva*:
"One should fill the vessels that have been placed between the *ghaṭa* and the *śrīpātra*, according to the sequence of the general *argha* offering, with the *kāraṇa* [liquor]."
Now follows the rule for the placement of the Śrīpātra:
O Supreme Goddess, the hero should place the Śrīpātra in front [of himself],
with its lines pointing eastward during the day and northward at night, according to the distinction between day and night.
In another tantra:
"O Maheśvarī, having filled the vessels according to the procedure for the general *argha*, one should place them facing north with their openings toward the west."

If one should perform the daytime ritual circle (divācakra), it should be directed either toward the east or the north; if one should perform the nighttime ritual circle (niśācakra), it should be directed toward the north or the west. (Nārāyaṇītantra 5)
127) Now, the enumeration of the vessels is stated in the *Yāmala*:
O Parameśānī, O Śivā, one should establish nine, seven, five, or three vessels with the mantra.
Now, the description of the names of the nine vessels.
In the *Yāmala*: "The vessel of the Goddess, the vessel of the Guru, and the vessel of enjoyment, O Maheśvarī..."
O Maheśvarī, the vessel for the yoginīs and the vessel for the śaktis.
The hero’s vessel, the vessel for water for the feet, the vessel for water for sipping,
and the ninth vessel— these are said to bestow the fruits of the four aims of human life.

Now follows the description of the names of the seven vessels: O Maheśvarī, the vessel for the Guru, the vessel for enjoyment, the vessel for the Śakti, the vessel for the Yoginīs, the vessel for the Vīras, and the seventh is indeed the vessel for the offering (bali) and the water for the feet (pādya).
Now, the description of the names of the five vessels:
O Śivā, the vessel of the Goddess, the vessel of the Guru, and the vessel of enjoyment—
these three, O Maheśvarī, along with the vessel for the offering to the Yoginīs, constitute the five vessels.

Now, regarding the three vessels: the vessel for the Goddess, the vessel for enjoyment, and the vessel for the Guru, O Maheśvarī—these three vessels must be prepared; one should not employ a single vessel.
One should not use a single vessel even if it belongs to Maheśvara himself;
for his mantra should be known as futile, since the ritual action involving the Śakti would likewise be in vain.
Indeed, one should practice the "single vessel" (ekapātra), for one's own body is permeated by Śakti; since in the Vāmā [path], there is neither prohibition nor injunction. || 13 ||
Nevertheless, O Supreme Goddess, the man of knowledge (*jñānin*) should not perform meditation (*dhyāna*).
For, O Mistress of the Gods, for one devoted to meditation, the meditation upon the Guru is indeed the seed.
One should joyfully drink from a single vessel the wine produced from the Guru’s vessel. || 14 ||
In the *Kubjikātantra*:
"Taking up a single vessel, the devotee should drink wine as long as he experiences bliss, drinking it gradually, step by step. (15)
Now follows the explanation of the names of the vessels as stated in the Kubjikātantra:
the vessel of the Goddess, the vessel of the Guru, and the vessel of enjoyment— these three are considered [to be] the Yoginī-bali vessel, the worship vessel, and the self-vessel.
This is considered the five-vessel [rite]. || 16 ||
O Maheśvarī, the vessel for the Śakti, the vessel for the Vīra, and the seven vessels are proclaimed;
the water for the feet (pādya) and the water for sipping (ācamanīya) are celebrated as the ninth. || 17 ||
Now, the sequence for the offering of vessels:
One should offer the Goddess-vessel to the Goddess, the Guru-vessel to the Guru, and the enjoyment-vessel to the Śakti; from the worship-vessel, one should worship Śivā. (18)
One should offer the vessel of the self into the mouth of the Kulakundalinī;
the vessel of the Śakti to the Śakti alone, and the vessel of the Vīra to the Vīra. (19)

O Dear One, one should offer the vessel for foot-water at the feet and the water for rinsing the mouth in the mouth; furthermore, one should worship with the nectar from the Śrīpātra, or with the arghya and other offerings.
In the *Yāmala*: "One should give the vessel of the Goddess to the Goddess; the vessel of the Guru to the Guru;
and for the sake of enjoyment, one should cause the vessel of enjoyment to be given to the Śakti. (21)
O Mistress of the Kula, one should offer the vessel of the Yoginī to the Yoginī,
and present the vessel of the bali offering to Vaṭuka and the Kṣetrapālas.

(129) One should offer the vessel for the Śakti to the Śakti, and the vessel for the Vīra to the Vīra; the vessel for foot-water at the feet of the Goddess, and the vessel for water for sipping in her mouth. || 23 ||
O beautiful lady, one should offer all else as nectar from the *śrīpātra*;
for the purpose of drinking the nectar of the feet, one should place the *kāraṇa* upon the feet.
Indeed, the *kāraṇa* becomes the effect within the lotus-feet of the Śrī Devī.
In the Viṣṇuyāmala:
"O Goddess, when the causal [mantra] is indeed conjoined with the feet of the Śrīdevī, the practitioner, having abandoned the state of death, becomes immortal. (25)
One should drink the remnant of the Śakti within the Cakra, for the chewing [of the offering] is indeed the remnant of the Vīras;
therefore, all practitioners should place the Kāraṇa into their mouths.
In the *Jñānārṇava*:
"O Supreme Goddess, at the end of the wheel, one should offer water for sipping (*ācamanīyaka*);
at its conclusion, O Goddess, the practitioner should drink the honey from the lower lip. (27)
In the *Nigamakalpalatā*: "O Śaṅkara, wherever there is a Śrīcakra, there I go;
residing within a woman’s body, I partake of the drinking of nectar. (28)
In her suffering I am also suffering, and in her happiness I share in that happiness;
just as when the body suffers, the embodied soul becomes a partaker of suffering. (29)
Even the single goddess Sundarī is threefold within the Śrīcakras;
for the sake of the practitioner's liberation, she is anointed with wine and accompanied by a lover. (30)
Sundarī, possessing the form of a beautiful woman, is the supreme sovereign of the lords of kings;
she is the supreme Śrī Kālikā in form, the excellent one for the protection of the Śrīcakra.
With a sword in hand, with a lolling tongue, with loose hair, and four arms; granting boons and fearlessness, endowed with a terrible roar, and adorned with ornaments. (32)
Holding the hand of her own lord, the Cakrapālikā wanders about;
naked and intoxicated, the Great Goddess sits upon a corpse on the back of a lion.
The Yoginī, joined in yoga, holding a sword in her hand and naked, accompanied by hundreds of thousands [of attendants], shall always protect the Śrīcakra. || 34 ||
The supreme Vidyā Śrītārī resides within the Śrīcakra, supported by material substances;
she bestows the bliss of drinking upon sight, smell, and touch. || 35 ||
Having taken up the full cup, one should place it upon the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila).
At the conclusion of the worship, one should offer the vessel to Śakti; she, being filled with compassion, should accept it.
Thus ends the thirty-second chapter in the Sarvollāsa composed by Śrī Sarvānandanātha. || 0 ||
The Thirty-third Chapter:
Now, the *vaṭuka-bali*.
In the *Kulārṇava*:
O Kuleśvarī, as long as one does not offer a vessel to the Vaṭuka, all the gods remain unsatisfied; yet, O Śivā, they are satisfied through mere remembrance and worship.
One should worship Vaṭuka and the others in the circle with perfumes, flowers, and so forth, in due order;
then, one should offer the vessel containing all the ritual substances while reciting the mantra.
p. 131) [In this regard, the following reading is found in the Dha, Cha, and Ja manuscripts:
— Now, the mantra of Vaṭuka.]
Oṃ oṃ oṃ! O Devīputra Vaṭukanātha, you who possess a mass of tawny matted hair, who are radiant, tawny-eyed, three-eyed, and flame-mouthed, accept, accept this bali offering, svāhā!
May Vaṭuka, satisfied by the offering of the bali, grant all accomplishments.

May he, who is served by spirits and *vetālas*, grant me constant peace. Now follows the extraction of the *vaṭuka* mantra from the *Jñānārṇava*: [The mantra is: *oṃ vaṭukāya āpaduddharaṇāya kuru kuru vaṣaṭ*.
In the *Jñānārṇava*: [it is stated: "One should worship Vaṭuka, who is surrounded by a multitude of *bhūtas*, *piśācas*, and *vetālas*, with offerings of meat, liquor, and blood."
Come, come, O Son of the Goddess! O End of the Vaṭuka! O Lord! O End of Kapila! O Mass of Matted Hair! O Radiant One! O Three-eyed One! || 3 ||
And at the very end: "O Jvālāmukha, destroy, destroy the obstacles!
Accept this offering accompanied by all ritual services!"—this mantra of Vaṭuka, ending with the wife of Vahni (Svāhā), has been proclaimed.
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ, come, come, O Son of the Goddess, Vaṭukanātha, you who possess a mass of tawny matted hair, the radiant three-eyed one, Jvālāmukha! Destroy, destroy the obstacles! Accept this bali-offering accompanied by all ritual services.
Take it, svāhā!
May Vaṭuka, who is satisfied by the offering of the bali and who bestows all perfections, and who is attended by spirits and vetālas, grant me constant peace. (5)
[In this regard, this reading is found in the Gha, Cha, and Ja manuscripts:
Oṃ oṃ oṃ! To all the Yoginīs, to all the Bhūtas, to the Ḍākinīs, to the Śākinīs, to those who dwell in the three worlds, accept, accept this offering of worship, svāhā!]
Now, the offering to the Yoginīs: Whether above the cosmic egg, or in heaven, in the expanse of the sky,
on the surface of the earth, in the partless [void], or in the netherworld, in fire, in water, in air, or wherever else it may be situated—

May the goddesses, who have taken their places in the sacred fields, seats, and secondary seats through offerings of incense, lamps, and the like, and who are worshipped by the lords of gods, always protect us with their favor through the rite of the auspicious bali offering. (6)
Oṃ! To all the yoginīs, to all the bhūtas, to the ḍākinīs, to those who dwell in the three worlds: accept, accept this offering of worship, svāhā!
Oṃ yāṃ, to the Yoginīs, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
The extraction of this [mantra] is as follows:
at the end of this, O Maheśānī, one should write the seed-syllable *yām*, then *yoginībhyaḥ svāhā*; at the end of all the syllables, one should write the word *yoginī*. || 7 ||
Having written the armor (kavaca) and the weapon (astra), one should again write the consort of fire (vahnijāyā).
O Goddess, by means of this mantra, an offering (bali) for the Yoginīs shall be accomplished.
Oṃ! Whosoever are the Yoginīs—whether Rudras, gentle, most terrible, or supreme;
whether moving in the sky or moving on the earth—may they always be pleased with me. (9)
[In this regard, this variant reading is seen in the Gha, Cha, and Ja manuscripts:
Oṃ oṃ oṃ! O God of gods, son of the Goddess, Vaṭukanātha! O Ucchiṣṭahāriṇī! Again and again, kṣaṃ kṣaṃ! O Kṣetrapāla, destroy, destroy all obstacles!]
"Accept, accept this series of offerings accompanied by all ritual services, svāhā!
Now follows the offering to the Kṣetrapāla: O Dear One, one should write the syllable *kṣa*, which is differentiated by the six long vowels.
One should also draw the locations, fields, and positions, as well as the drinking vessels, incense, lamps, and so forth.
Having drawn the figure of Vali together with his attendants, one should then say, "Seize, seize!
O beautiful one, this is the mantra of Kṣetrapāla, joined with the wife of Vahni (the svāhā-utterance).
The mantra is:
Oṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ, come, come, O Kṣetrapāla!
"Accept, accept this offering together with incense, lamps, and so forth, svāhā!
He who dwells in this field and is a servant of the Kṣetrapāla—may he, being pleased by this gift of an offering, grant me protection from all [harm]. || 12 ||
[This reading is not found in the manuscripts G, CH, and J. Now, the Gaṇeśa-bali:
having written the triad GĀM, GĪM, GŪM, followed by Gaṇapati ending in the nasal Ṅ.
At the end of "vara," at the end of "varada," and at the end of "sarva," one should write "jana."

Having uttered, "Bring [him] under my control," and "Accept the offering (bali)," the mantra of Gaṇeśa, ending with the wife of Vahni (svāhā) and containing the two-word phrase, shall take away the offering.
[This reading is not found in the manuscripts G, C, and J.
The mantra, however, is:
*gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaṇapataye varavarada sarvajanaṃ me vaśaṃ cālaya*.
Accept the offering, accept it, svāhā!
Now, the offering to all beings:
Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ! Salutation to all beings, the lords of all beings and their leaders.
Those beings of various forms who dwell in the quarters, on the earth, and in the intermediate space.
And those residing in the depths of Pātāla were addressed by means of Śiva-yoga. || 15 ||
May Dhruva and the others, all the Gandharvas, Indra and all the deities, and all beings with joyful minds, be satisfied; may they accept this bali offering. 16.
(p. 134) Now follows the general offering (*sāmānyabali*).
This offering to the Lord of the Kings of Kings is approved by all the gods.
The deity desires the sacrificial offering (bali) for which a name must be assigned.
Afterwards, one should utter the three *tāra*s (oṃ āḥ hūṃ), then "Amuka Kṣetrapālaka," and thereafter "O Rājarājeśvara, accept this offering of worship (*pūjāvali*).
Then follows the pair "gṛhṇa" twice, ending with the word "toya. This mantra bestows all fruits. || 18 ||
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ oṃ oṃ, O Kṣetrapāla [Name], Lord of the Kings of Kings, accept, accept this offering of worship, svāhā!
By this offering, may the Lord, the Sovereign of the Kings of Kings, together with his assembly of young attendants, be forever gracious to me. (19)
[Verses 20–23 are not found in the manuscripts G, C, H, and J.
The offering for Vaṭuka should be made with the left thumb and ring finger;
that for the Yoginīs is said to be made with the right thumb and ring finger. (20)
In the Dakṣiṇāmūrtisaṃhitā:
"First, having formed the left fist, make the index finger the refuge.
O Goddess, by means of this mudrā, the offering to the Kṣetrapāla shall be accomplished. (21)
Likewise, place the middle finger among the clenched fingers like a staff;
this great mudrā called Gajatuṇḍa shall be the offering for Gaṇeśa.
By this offering of bali, those accompanied by the host of young attendants [shall be satisfied].
May the Goddess Rājarājeśvarī be gracious to me at all times. || 23 ||
In the *Kumārikā-tantra*:
Now follows the exposition of the Lamp of the Kula.
O Great Goddess, in the rite of the Kula, one should cause the Kula-lamp to be offered;
for without the Kula-lamp, O auspicious lady, the lamp of knowledge will never arise anywhere. (24)
The Goddess said:
"O beloved of my life, tell me: what is the form of the lamp of the Kula, by what substance is it made, and in what form is the offering to be presented?"
Śrī Śiva said:
One should fashion triangular pits with slightly reddened flour,
and lamps the size of the nail of an old man, along with hand-drums (ḍamarukas).
O Great Goddess, one should arrange lamps numbering nine, seven, three, five, or ten thousand, or fewer than a hundred, in pairs according to one's capacity. (27)
O Supreme Goddess, having circumambulated the lamp one hundred times more than a thousand,
with pairs of lamps, one should dissolve one's own radiance into the [divine] radiance.
In the *Jñānārṇava*:
"A practitioner devoted to the Kula should offer a thousand Kula-lamps at night during Kula-rites, and a hundred lamps during rites performed by day. (29)
O Maheśvarī, having unified the inner light and the outer light into one,
and having whirled it three times before the Goddess, one should offer the Kula-lamp.
The mantra is as follows:
"O Goddess, accept this lamp, which is my very self, joined with the Mistress of all the wheels [cakras], deep red in color, and bestowing desires, for the sake of my accomplishment. (31)
One should show the lamp three times, bowing from the feet up to the head;
or specifically, on the fifth, seventh, or ninth occasion. (32)
In the *Kālīvilāsatantra*: Now follows the acceptance of the vessel (*pātrasvīkāra*).
First, one should worship one’s chosen deity (*iṣṭadevī*) with water for the feet (*pādya*) and other offerings.
By those who move within form;
then one should worship Śakti in the wheel, by which Śakti one is united with Śiva (or the Beloved).

One should worship Śivā with the mantra taught in one's own respective Vidyā according to the prescribed rite; or, if they are initiated, one may worship Śivā as either one's own Śakti or another's Śakti.
Having worshipped it with the perception that it is a deity— or having meditated upon it— one should offer the vessel of enjoyments.
She, for her part, having paid homage to the vessel with the mudrā of the hollowed palms, [should accept] the vessel of the self.
Having grasped it with the trident mudrā, one should drink it according to the word of the teacher.
O Maheśvarī, one should also offer it to other Śaktis;
O Bhairavī, a separate vessel should be given along with honey.
Taking the vessel, that goddess should give the remnant of the vessel as a favor to Bhairava, to his devotee, and to his servant.
Having first taken the vessel and placed it with honey, O Dear One, one should worship the goddess Svaṣṭā and mutter the root mantra;
O Great Goddess, one should worship the goddess Surā with meat and ritual hand-gestures (mudrās). || 38 ||
Having performed the ritual assignment of the limbs (aṅganyāsa) as well as the assignment of the hands and limbs (karāṅganyāsa),
and having then performed breath control (prāṇāyāma), one should take up the excellent vessel.
In the Kubjikātantra:

O Maheśvarī, [one should perform] the placement of the limbs (aṅganyāsa), the placement of the hands (karanyāsa), the placement of the phonemes (varṇanyāsa), the placement of the seers (ṛṣinyāsa) as prescribed by one's own vidyā, and also the pervasive placement (vyāpakanyāsa). (40)
Relying upon the fivefold placement (nyāsa), one should joyfully perform breath control (prāṇāyāma).
Then, having paid homage to the vessel, one should offer oblation into the mouth of Kuṇḍalinī. || 41 ||
Thus ends the thirty-third chapter in the Sarvollāsa composed by Śrī Sarvānandanātha. || 0 ||
The Thirty-Fourth Chapter.
The venerable Goddess said:
"O beloved of my life, tell me: what is the fruit of the multitude of nyāsas?
And what is the fruit of prāṇāyāma, whose name is most exceedingly subtle?"
Now, the fruit of the ritual placement on the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*) and so forth.
Śrī Śiva said:
One should perform the ritual placement on the limbs and the ritual placement on the hands either with the root mantra or with the *praṇava*.
O Goddess, one should perform the deposition of the letters (varṇanyāsa) according to the fifty-fold Manu.
In the ritual assignment of the limbs (aṅganyāsa), one should contemplate the six limbs as the limbs of the deity;
in the ritual assignment of the hands (karanyāsa), the hand is to be known as merely the hand of the deity.
O Maheśānī, when the fifty forms of the Mātṛkās and millions upon millions of deities are assigned to the letters, the body becomes composed of the gods.

During the rite of Nyāsa for the sages (ṛṣinyāsa), one should indeed contemplate one’s own body as the body of the God; O Goddess of Gods, through that knowledge, one should contemplate "I am He," identifying oneself with the sage.
In another tantra:
"If one has grasped the mantra of the deity, and if the deity is truly present, then when that body is always perceived as the form of the deity, 'I am that'—this is knowledge. (6)
In the *Kubjikātantra*:
"Earth, water, fire, air, ether, as well as the embodied being and the mind [O Śivā]," (p. 138).
Through the network of sevenfold placements, these seven possess divine forms.
O Śivā, the practitioner of mantra, O wise one, should empower [the body] from the feet to the head seven times with the root mantra, performing the placement of the *kyāpa* [vowels].
Now, the fruit of *prāṇāyāma*:
O Queen of the Gods, by means of *prāṇāyāma*, Kuṇḍalī abandons even sleep;
O Mistress of the Kula, she accepts whatever is offered to her with devotion. (9)
O Śivā, one should take the vessel filled with the causal [substances] while reciting the mantra;
having placed it upon the support (ādhāra) with the mantra, one should thereafter perform the libation (tarpaṇa).
One should satisfy [the deities] together with the Guru from their respective vessels by means of the causal offerings;
having satisfied the Guru’s Śakti, one should then satisfy one’s own chosen Goddess.
Regarding the reality of the *nigama*:
O God, when one should contemplate one's own chosen Goddess as one's supreme power (*svaśakti*).
At that time, even for the sake of the Śakti, she is undoubtedly a fit vessel for the Goddess;
following the command of the Guru, he should engage in dalliance with that Śakti.
When one should contemplate one's own chosen goddess, red in color, situated to the left of one's own desired deity; O Supreme Lord, one should contemplate one's own Śakti as the chosen goddess.
Having offered the vessel according to the command of the Guru, one should perform the ritual action.
To a mere woman she would be the consort of Hara, and to a mere man he would be Śaṅkara;
marriage is to be understood as a bond, O beloved, like fire situated within a wick.
Lord Śiva is the Guru, and the Guru-deity is Sadāśiva himself;
at his left side is merely a woman, and her dalliance is by his command.
*Nārāyaṇītantra* (p. 139):
O Maheśānī, by whose command one should accomplish heroic deeds (*vīrakarmāṇi*).
By his command, one should take delight in the Śakti and abandon the notion of her being one's mother. || 16 ||
Now, the procedure for libation (*tarpaṇa*):
With meat mixed with *kāraṇa*, one should sprinkle a mere drop upon the head using both hands in the *tattva-mudrā*,
while reciting the *pādukā-mantra*.
Meditating on the feet of the glorious Guru upon his own head, he [should contemplate] the Guru’s sandals.
Having thus gratified the power of the Guru (guruśakti) as well as Ānandabhairavī,
one should indeed gratify the god Ānandabhairava and one's own chosen Vidyā.
One should offer libations three times upon the head and also three times upon the heart;
one should satisfy the Guru together with one's chosen mantra (vidyā) in the thousand-petalled lotus (sahasrāra).
One should satisfy the delightful deity within the heart by means of its differentiation;
O auspicious one, one should satisfy it in non-differentiation within the great city of the thousand-spoked wheel.
Through libation (tarpaṇa), there shall be peace, and the stability of the deities shall be secured;
therefore, one should offer libations to the gods in both Tantric and Vedic rites. (21)
As for the mantra:
having uttered the three *tāras* followed by the name of the venerable Guru, [one says], "O Dear One, I satisfy the venerable *pādukā*, or I worship it. (22)
Now, the libation to the lineage of gurus:
O Goddess, one should offer libations three times each to the Guru, the Paraguru, the Parāparaguru, and then the Parameṣṭhiguru. (23)
140) In the *Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi*, the illustrious Pārvatī said:
"O Supreme Lord, who is the Guru? Could there be anyone who is the supreme Guru?"
Who is the supreme and subordinate guru, and who is the preceptor of the highest station? || 24 ||
The illustrious Śiva said:
The unity of both the gross and the subtle is the cause of knowledge;
the gross alone has various forms, just as fire is when conjoined with wood.
The cognition of the subtle should be understood as the seed of the cognition of the gross;
the cognition of the gross should be understood as the seed of the cognition of the subtle.
Having unified the gross and the subtle, all this has been revealed. (26)
The giver of the mantra is called the Guru, while the mantra itself is the supreme Guru;
you indeed are the higher and lower Guru, and I am the Parameṣṭhi Guru.
Now, the libation (tarpaṇa) for one’s own chosen deity.
In the *Haṃsamāheśvara*:
"First, having uttered the root mantra, [one should offer it] along with the weapons and the retinue."
I satisfy my own chosen goddess together with her vehicle in two ways; [I am] Antaka. || 28 ||
For the seed of the knowledge of unity is indeed devoid of both prohibition and injunction;
yet, if one should satisfy the future [consort] through attachment to ritual action, she should be satisfied together with the Guru. (29)
One should meditate on the white Guru, compassionate and accompanied by Śakti;
she is white in color, two-armed, adorned, two-eyed, and united with him. (30)

One should meditate upon the Guru as being joined with her— who is red in passion (rajas) and black in darkness (tamas), possessing four arms and three eyes— and one should perform the libation (tarpaṇa) and other rites.
p. 141) Then follows the sequence.
In the Jñānārṇava:
One should perform the libation with the left hand by joining the thumb and the ring finger;
with the right hand, one should cast the flower by joining the thumb and the forefinger.
The thumb is the deity Bhairava, and the ring finger is Caṇḍikā;
by the mere union of these two, the substance becomes like nectar.
The thumb is also Bhairava, and the index finger is the supreme Caṇḍikā.
By the mere union of these two, the substance becomes a captivating flower.
O Śaṅkarī, the index finger of the right hand takes the form of Caṇḍikā;
through its union with the thumb, that goddess becomes flower-adorned and overwhelmed by desire. 35.
Holding [the vessel] with the right hand and likewise with the *tattvamudrā* in the left,
one should perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*) with the *mūla-mantra*, using only meat as the substance. Thereafter, having grasped the *yoni-mudrā*, one should offer the libation within the *yoni*.
Even by causing a flower to fall into the womb with the right hand,
the passionate woman becomes satisfied with that substance consisting of a mere drop.
Even in the absence of one's own [physical] power, one should contemplate the source (yoni) within the water;
the libation and other rites must be performed, for water is the eternal Māyā. 38.
Just as a courtesan is worthy of honor by all and grants liberation from bondage to everyone, so too is water worthy of honor by all and grants liberation from bondage to everyone. (39)
In the *Jñānārṇava*:
"O Goddess, the wise one should perform the auspicious libation upon his own body, for his own body is the body of the God;
he should offer it as libation either on the crown of his head or in his heart. (40)
O Goddess, there is libation three times and the scattering of flowers three times;
when the three qualities are unified, the libation is performed once. (41)
Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter in the Sarvollāsa composed by Śrī Sarvānandanātha. || 0 ||
The Thirty-Fifth Chapter:
Now, the Acceptance of the Vessel.
Then, having paid homage to the vessel with the mudrā of the hollowed palms, [ch, j: and that vessel].
Taking hold with the trident mudrā, one performs the salutation at each vessel. || 1 ||
In the *Jñānadvīpa*:
"One should bow to the vessel of Śakti; Śakti is the vessel for the hero (*vīra*), and the hero is the vessel for Śakti.
One should contemplate the Goddess Surā as being present in each vessel, endowed with purity. (2)
Holding the vessel placed upon the support with the right hand, and placing it in the other, the left hand, one should pray to the goddess Surā. || 3 ||
Now, the prayer: When the ocean was being churned— the milk-ocean, the best of seas—
the Goddess Surā was born therein, the embodiment of the cause in the Kali age.
It is the nectar among the worlds of truth and the cause within the heavenly worlds.
"O Surā, grant me the state of being *suratva* (divinity) while I am overwhelmed by desire! By your touch you are the bestower of desires; by your sight you are the remover of sins;
by your service you are bliss itself; and through union with you, O lovely one, you are liberation. (5)
O Maheśvarī, there may be three vessels, five vessels, or seven vessels; O Goddess,
the ninth vessel is to be honored, and one should drink the honey-liquor from it.
One should never have a vessel made with a single bowl or a pair of bowls at the edge of the rim;
a vessel devoid of the prescribed number brings nothing but death.
In another tantra:
"O Goddess, if Maheśvara himself is present, one must not use a single vessel;
his mantra is in vain, and the drinking [of liquor] bestows hell. (8)
In the Kulārṇava:
"One should drink the honey (madhu) according to the rule, beginning with three vessels and ending with five.
Beyond this, O Maheśānī, what rule could possibly be effective?"
If there were a fixed rule up to the seventh or the ninth [day], then one should not observe a restrictive vow until that time. || 10 ||
O Pārvatī, I shall explain its meaning, the salutation, and the mantra; listen.
O Maheśvarī, five vessels are to be saluted, and the ninth as well.
One should perform the salutation in the proper sequence and drink the honey according to the rule.
Now, the salutation with five vessels (*pañcapātravandana*):
[I salute the deity] who is bathed by the nectar of the moon shining from the crest of the glorious Bhairava,
and who is worshipped by the hosts of *siddhas*, the *yoginīs*, and the assemblies of the lords of the sacred fields (*kṣetrādhīśvara*).
I salute this great-souled ocean of bliss, the manifest nectar of the three worlds, the first glorious hand-water that bestows purity upon the vessel of the universe. 12.
"I offer [this] into the mouth of Kuṇḍalī; drink!"—thus should the Guru say. Having meditated upon Kuṇḍalinī as far as the tip of the tongue, he should partake of the honeyed drink.
In the *Tantracintāmaṇi*:
"O Pārvatī, [holding] the cup in the left hand with the right hand..."
Having performed the purification, O Great Goddess, one should place it into the cup. || 14 ||
O Śivā, one should offer the vessel with the root mantra and receive it with the mantra of honey;
having offered it into the mouth of the Kulakuṇḍalinī, one should personally meditate upon the Guru.
Again, O Mistress of the Family, having taken the vessel containing meat, one should offer it into the mouth by means of the root mantra as Kuṇḍalinī; this is the definition of Brahman. (16)
Second Veneration of the Vessel | Second Veneration of the Vessel | Oṃ! [The vessel] made of gold, bringing the essence of fish, and offered by my beloved along with drinks and other delicacies.
Something was communicated to her by her with eyes like trembling, red lotuses,
having set before her on the left a sweet drink that brings about purification, which was her very self.
Now I salute the second vessel, which increases sole bliss. || 17 ||
The third salutation to the vessel:
It is endowed with the entire collection of the arts of all traditions, and it illuminates [the essence of] wonder.
It is served by Candra, Upendra, Mahendra, Śambhu, Varuṇa, Brahmā, and others;
it is meditated upon at all times by the hosts of gods, by the hosts of sages, and by Brahmā and others who seek liberation.
Now I salute the third vessel, which removes sin and is capable of awakening the self.
